snippets.title: The goal — one manager, three programs, every paid visit verified
snippets.narration: Connect lets one person oversee several programs at once and act on all of them from a single place — confident that every service being paid for has actually been verified. Here, one manager oversees three network managers running RUTF distribution and weekly MUAC screening. From one screen she checks each manager's SOP compliance, opens a flagged worker's audited photos and the coaching that followed, and tracks an individual child's recovery — every number backed by the verified visit behind it.
snippets.sentence: One program manager can oversee three network managers running RUTF and MUAC screening from a single Program Admin Report, and reach the primary record behind any number she is paying for.

snippets.title: Priya sees the whole program at a glance
snippets.narration: Priya opens the Program Admin Report and sees all three network managers on one grid — four weeks each, with an aggregate that calls out who is meeting the screening SOP. Northern is clean; Central and Eastern both read below.
snippets.sentence: The Program Admin Report renders all three network managers' weekly reviews as one grid of week cells with a pinned per-manager aggregate, so the program manager reads the whole program's SOP compliance before opening any individual review.

snippets.title: Priya clicks into a resolved week in Central's row
snippets.narration: She clicks a resolved week in Central's row. An inline panel names the worker who was flagged — Kadi Fofana — and links straight to the audit and the coaching task that dealt with it, without leaving the report.
snippets.sentence: Clicking a resolved week cell opens an inline detail panel under that cluster's row that names each flagged worker and links their audit and coaching task, without navigating away from the report.

snippets.title: Priya opens the run behind the cell
snippets.narration: She opens the review behind the cell — Bakary's own weekly nutrition review, the per-worker table with its MUAC distribution and SAM and MAM rates, its action buttons now reporting what was already done.
snippets.sentence: The detail panel's 'Open the run' link lands on the network manager's underlying weekly review, whose action buttons are state-aware — rows with an existing audit or task show View buttons instead of Create menus.

snippets.title: Priya checks the child's MUAC photos the auditor saw
snippets.narration: She opens the audit and sees the child's MUAC photos herself — each screened child's assessment photo with the auditor's pass-or-fail decision, all on one page.
snippets.sentence: The View Audit drill lands on the completed audit session where each screened child's MUAC photo and its per-photo pass or fail decision are visible on one page.

snippets.title: Priya reads the coaching that turned the numbers around
snippets.narration: She reads the closed coaching conversation — the full transcript on the task — and watches that worker's screening numbers recover week over week after the manager stepped in.
snippets.sentence: A closed coaching task retains its full AI coaching transcript on the task page, and that transcript shows the flagged worker's screening profile recovering week over week after the network manager intervened.

snippets.title: Now the harder case — Central's still-open week
snippets.narration: Then the harder cell. Central's still-open week separates a worker whose case is closed from one still under investigation, naming the specific open audit and task.
snippets.sentence: An open-work cell's detail panel distinguishes flagged workers whose cases are closed from those still under investigation, naming the specific open audit and task records.

snippets.title: Priya inspects the audit still in review
snippets.narration: She opens the in-review audit — MUAC photo cards in mixed states, still reading Save Progress rather than Complete Image Review until every child's photo has a decision.
snippets.sentence: An in-review audit page shows per-photo progress and offers 'Save Progress' instead of 'Complete Image Review' until every child's MUAC photo has a decision.

snippets.title: Priya checks on the coaching mid-conversation
snippets.narration: The coaching task is still open — its conversation in progress and the Close Task action still available, so the state of an unresolved case is readable straight from the task.
snippets.sentence: An open coaching task shows its in-progress conversation transcript and keeps its Close Task action available, so the state of an unresolved case is readable directly from the task page.

snippets.title: The third manager — an AI-caught misleading-photo case
snippets.narration: The third manager. Eastern's flagged cell surfaces a worker the AI image review caught submitting misleading MUAC photos — a different fate from a coached-to-close flag or an open case: suspended.
snippets.sentence: Clicking Eastern's flagged cell surfaces a worker the AI image review caught submitting misleading MUAC photos and whose coaching task closed as a suspension, a different fate from a coached-to-close or a still-open case.

snippets.title: Priya opens the audit and sees what the AI flagged
snippets.narration: She opens that audit and sees what the AI flagged — the reviewer's own per-photo verdict, a Hyperzoomed badge on the photos where the child's arm isn't visible, so she is verifying the machine's finding against the images, not just a status label.
snippets.sentence: The audit behind Vida's suspension shows the MUAC AI reviewer's own per-photo verdict — a "Hyperzoomed" badge on the flagged photos where the child's arm is not visible — so the program manager verifies the machine's finding against the images, not just a status label.

snippets.title: Priya returns to the aggregate and makes her call
snippets.narration: She lands back on the aggregate — Northern meeting the SOP, Central and Eastern below, each with runs, flags, and outcomes side by side — the contrast that decides where her week goes.
snippets.sentence: The aggregate column summarizes each network manager's window with an SOP MET or BELOW verdict plus run, flag, and outcome counts, making the three managers' health directly comparable on one screen.

snippets.title: Priya follows one child's recovery
snippets.narration: And to see what all that oversight is ultimately for, she follows one child. The SAM follow-up timeline drills to a single child's MUAC climbing across eight visits — out of red, through yellow, into green. Recovered.
snippets.sentence: The SAM Follow-up Timeline tracks every flagged child's MUAC across their follow-up visits, so the program manager can watch one child climb from red (SAM) through yellow (MAM) to green (recovered) over the review period — the oversight loop closing on a child, not a metric.
